4. By his judgment and order dated 27.8.70 the Company Judge allowed the application and gave direction to rectify the share register of the Company by deleting 630 shares in question allotted to the appellants. As regards service of notice under certificate of posting the learned Company Judge held that the presumption of service being not available in the absence of registered service and the appellants having failed to prove due service of notice upon the respondents, their plea of proper service of notice could not be acceptable. Against this order the appellants preferred an appeal, Company Appeal No. 4 of 1970, which was dismissed with costs. The learned Judges of the High Court Division observed as follows: 

 "It is true that the Article does not require that notice is to be sent by registered post, but in order to avail of the benefits of the presumption under section 114 of the Evidence Act, ordinary service under certificate of posting is not sufficient unless notice is sent by registered post, the statutory presumption is not available''. 

 I. Because in view of the provision in the Article of Association of the Company prescribing the mode of service of notice regulations 49 and 112 of the Companies Act, the learned Judges of the High Court Division are not justified in holding with reference to section 27 of the General Clauses Act that notice is to be sent by registered post so as to avail of statutory presumption as to service and that ordinary service under certificate of posting is not sufficient. 

 6. Mr. "Khondker Mahhubuddin Ahmed, counsel for the appellant’s, submitted that in view of the provisions of the Articles of Association of the Company which are based on the provisions of the Companies Act and the liptigned notices having been served accordion such provisions, the learned Judges were wrong in holding that the presumptions of section 114 of the Evidence Act was not available since the impugned notices were not sent by registered post, certificate of posting being not sufficient to raise the presumption under the aforesaid section. 

 11. It was emphatically asserted by the appellants learned counsel that this being proper service, the notices must be accepted to have been served on the share holders even though they were not sent by registered post. The learned counsel for the appellants submitted that the presumption of service was available in case of service of notice under certificate of posting as well. 

 12. According to the learned Judges of the High Court Division service of notice under certificate of posting does not raise the presumption under section 114 of Evidence Act. In order to avail of the presumption under the aforesaid section notice has to be sent by registered post, service under certificate of posting being not sufficient Mr. Nurullah, counsel for the respondents, asserted that in view of the provisions of section 27 of the General Clauses Act which were also taken into consideration by the learned Judges of the High Court Division the presumption claimed by the appellants was not available. Section 27 of the General Clauses Act reads as follows: 

 13. Reading the relevant provisions of the Articles of Association of the Company and Regulation 112 as well as section 27 of the general Clauses Act, it appears that when a notice is claimed to have been served by post, the presumption of service of such notice will be raised if the notice was sent by registered post. Such presumption is, however, neither conclusive nor irrefutable. In other words, the person to whom the letter or notice is addressed is at liberty to prove that it was not in fact served upon, nor received by him. Even though no presumption arises in case of a letter sent under certificate of posting, the respondents have been found to have proved that no such notices were even received by them. Excepting the claim that the notices of the impugned Board meeting were sent to the respondents under certificate of posting, the appellants have not succeeded in meeting the challenge of the respondents that they were never received by them by producing evidence to that effect. We, therefore, find no reason to differ from the views expressed by the learned Judges of the High Court Division regarding non-availability of the Statutory presumption of service, and this being so the conclusions raised by them must be upheld.
